WHICH COUNTRY DOES NATURE HIT THE HARDEST

Japan gets crushed by earthquakes, about 1,500 a year, and the tsunamis that follow. 

The US sees the world’s most tornadoes in Tornado Alley. 

Indonesia tops volcanic eruptions on the Ring of Fire. 

The Philippines takes nearly 20 cyclones a year, making it the most vulnerable nation on the World Risk Index.

But if you count everything together, the United States is nature’s favorite target: hurricanes, tornadoes, quakes, droughts, wildfires, even volcanoes. 

Source: @geoglobe_tales

🚨🇯🇵 JAPAN ROCKED BY 1,600 QUAKES IN 3 WEEKS, ISLANDERS FORCED TO FLEE

Japan’s remote southern islands have been rattled by nearly 1,600 earthquakes since June 21, shaking nerves and sending dozens fleeing Akuseki Island, though major damage has luckily been avoided so far.

Seismologists blame an underwater volcano and magma flows but admit they have zero clue when the shaky saga will stop.

Meanwhile, a manga’s doomsday prediction for July 5 flopped spectacularly, but tourists are still spooked, proving that fiction sometimes hits harder than a 5.1 quake.
